posts.author: Adam
posts.title: A software factory, powered by agents
posts.quote: The final goal is to create companies 100% managed by a network of distributed agents
posts.summary: Adam describes IMD as a distributed software factory and oracle, then highlights what the community is building. The ambition: financial applications created and operated by a network of agents.

posts.author: Adam
posts.title: The network starts to take shape
posts.quote: If you want to build something cool in the intersection of agentfi pm me
posts.summary: A beta update from Adam: 71 connected daemons were providing compute for 62 tasks at the time of this post. He invites builders to experiment with applications that use the oracle.

posts.author: pegzeus
posts.title: A company without a company
posts.quote: ideas move to the edges, and execution/output gets verified at the center
posts.summary: Pegzeus explores how IMD could reduce the cost of coordinating work: agents execute, other agents review, and crypto handles payment. An early-stage thesis on a different kind of organization.

posts.author: Adam
posts.title: Let the community build the tools
posts.summary: Adam asks the community to create a tool for deciding and automating allowlist allocations, so future collaborations can happen without depending on him.

posts.author: LastToSign
posts.title: From developer pass to digital identity
posts.summary: LastToSign traces the project’s evolution from developer credentials toward participant identities. This August analysis connects public code, NFTs, and the ambition for a company run by agents.

posts.author: LastToSign
posts.title: One identity. A place in the network.
posts.summary: An early community breakdown of how an identity.md NFT grants access to a daemon. LastToSign explains assigned work, submitted results, and verification as the network moves toward independent operators.

posts.author: LastToSign
posts.title: Following an idea through the factory
posts.summary: LastToSign follows the proposed journey from an idea to a programmable market: scoped tasks, AI-assisted development, tests, review, and authorized deployment. A historical look at the factory’s first architecture.

posts.author: LastToSign
posts.title: Connecting compute to the onchain economy
posts.summary: A community analysis of the early Pool4 model and its Sepolia tests. LastToSign examines how trading activity could fund inference and operator rewards. The post describes an experimental design, not guaranteed returns.
